sovereign_country.strategic_role: 极速离岸证券与外汇交易商持牌（VFSC）、轻资产免税出海

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Vanuatu Financial Intelligence Unit Act No. 34 of 2012 (as amended); Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act No. 2 of 2014 (AML/CFT Act); International Companies Act No. 32 of 1993 (as amended), Chapter 222; Companies (Amendment) Act 2012 introducing UBO reporting obligations; VFSC Regulatory Directives on Beneficial Ownership, Financial Crimes Investigation Division (FID) guidelines.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all proposed directors, shareholders, UBOs, and beneficial owners against: United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals List, EU/UK consolidated sanctions lists, Australian DFAT sanctions list, and Vanuatu FIU domestic watchlist (list compiled under AML/CFT Act, section 4). A formal PEP status declaration and enhanced due diligence (EDD) is mandatory for any politically exposed person, family member, or close associate. Screening must occur pre-incorporation and be documented by the VFSC registered agent; results retained for at least 7 years. Failure to disclose or false screening declarations result in rejection of incorporation and referral to the FIU for criminal investigation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) Company Name Reservation and Registration Online Portal (access via VFSC Registry Portal: https://www.vfsc.vu)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Statutory name requirements under International Companies Act, section 34: Company name must be distinct from any existing registered or reserved name in Vanuatu; may be in English or French, but must use Latin alphabet characters (A-Z, 0-9, and limited symbols); names must end with a mandatory suffix 'Limited', 'Incorporated', 'Corporation', or the abbreviation 'Ltd.', 'Inc.', 'Corp.'; foreign-language names must be transliterated into the Latin alphabet; use of Bislama or other scripts requires transliteration into English/French; the company name must not imply connection with the Government of Vanuatu or any foreign government absent ministerial consent.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: International Company (as suffix without qualifying for IC status)
Any name that suggests a regulated activity under VFSC licensing laws
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the proposed name is rejected by the VFSC Registrar, the applicant or registered agent must file a written Notice of Appeal with the VFSC Registration Committee within 14 calendar days of the rejection notification, stating the grounds of appeal and providing evidence that the name does not contravene section 34 restrictions and is not misleading. The fee for an appeal is VUV 10,000 (approx. USD 85) payable to the VFSC. The Committee will review and respond in writing within 21 business days. If no response is received or the appeal is denied, a fresh name application may be submitted with a new reservation fee. No judicial appeal is available at this pre-incorporation stage, but administrative review by the Vanuatu Ombudsman may be pursued for procedural unfairness.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is generally permissible for the registered agent relationship; however, the International Company must maintain a registered office address in Vanuatu as provided by the licensed registered agent. For a LegalTech SaaS conducting primarily cloud-based operations, the use of a virtual office for correspondence is acceptable, but the registered agent must have a physical office in Port Vila or Luganville. The company must also maintain adequate commercial substance in Vanuatu, which for an exempt International Company may be minimal but must include a registered agent, at least one director (may be non-resident), and a statutory filing record. If the company seeks to operate a physical service in Vanuatu, it must retain a lease and local staff, but such substance is not mandatory for pure SaaS export business.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low to Moderate: VFSC and Vanuatu FIU conduct periodic compliance inspections on registered agents, not directly on passive International Companies. However, if the registered agent is selected for an AML/CFT audit, the agent may require the company to provide information and may conduct a desktop verification. Unannounced physical on-site inspections of the registered office are rare for a low-risk SaaS company; estimated likelihood below 5% per year for a purely passive IC, but increases to approximately 15% if the company is linked to financial transactions or payment processing that triggers a review by the FIU.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act No. 32 of 1992, as amended by the International Companies (Amendment) Act 2011, Cap 222; applicable provisions include ss. 4–8 (incorporation requirements), s. 24 (registered office), ss. 39–40 (directors and secretary), and s. 42 (memorandum and articles).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) — Registry of International Companies
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Incorporation of an International Company (Form IC-01) together with the Memorandum and Articles of Association
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is prescribed under the International Companies Act; no escrow account or capital contribution deposit is required. Shares may be issued in any currency, fully or partly paid, as stipulated in the articles.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) That the subscribers to the Memorandum and Articles of Association hereby take up the initial share subscription as set forth in the register of members; (2) That the registered office of the Company in Vanuatu is adopted as [Registered Office Address], with the appointed Registered Agent for service of process; (3) That the first directors are appointed, and their appointments are effective immediately; (4) That all borrowings, bank account openings, and routine operational contracts necessary for the electronic signature and document automation business are hereby authorized; (5) That the secretary is appointed; (6) That the directors are authorized to execute all statutory filings with VFSC and do all things necessary to complete incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission — Name Approval Window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit 2–3 proposed company names via VFSC electronic portal, ensuring each name ends with 'Limited' or approved abbreviation. Pay the name search fee and obtain reservation confirmation before filing the incorporation application.
required_dossiers: Declaration of proposed company name availability
Identification of applicant or local agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a name is rejected as undesirable, confusing, or too similar to an existing company, submit a written appeal within 14 days or file an alternative name promptly; VFSC may approve an amended name without additional reservation delay.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: VU Registered Agent and Notary Public
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Memorandum and Articles of Association under the International Companies Act, including share capital structure, registered office, object clause, and director powers. Arrange subscriber signatures and director consent forms before a notary public; the documents must remain in English or Bislama as accepted by the Registry.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If VFSC returns the documents for correction, amend the defective clause and re-execute before the notary; the agent may resubmit under the same reference number without re-payment of incorporation fees where the defect is formal only.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Incorporation Application to VFSC
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission — Registry of International Companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form IC-01 through the VFSC online submission portal, attaching the executed constitutional documents, particulars of directors and secretary, registered office detail, and proof of registered agent acceptance. Ensure all fields are complete and fees are allocated to the Ministry of Finance consolidated revenue.
required_dossiers: Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association
Particulars of directors (full name, address, nationality, occupation)
Registered office consent from the local service provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, address the requisition letter within 14 days by amended filing or supplementary declaration. If VFSC objects to any wording, the registered agent may submit a revised constitutional document under a ministerial cover letter; refusal may be appealed to the VFSC Appeals Committee within 21 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Allocation and Share Subscription Record
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: International Company's Board of Directors and Registered Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Record initial share subscriptions in the register of members. Issue share certificates to subscribers. Unless the articles provide otherwise, capital may be issued as no-par value shares. A statutory declaration confirming no unlawful bearer shares is prepared for the VFSC file.
required_dossiers: Register of members and share ledgers
Resolution of directors on allotment of shares
Statutory declaration of beneficial ownership and bearer share prohibition
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If VFSC raises concerns over share ownership disclosure, file corrective declarations or disallow the noncompliant share class by board resolution and amend the articles accordingly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon successful vetting, VFSC issues the Certificate of Incorporation, accepting the registered office and confirming the company is an International Company. The certificate number and dated incorporation are entered into the Company's statutory records.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate is delayed due to internal VFSC backlog, file a written reminder through the licensed registered agent; if the issuance is declined, request an administrative review or re-file an unambiguous application within the statutory period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of Registered Office and Corporate Book Completion
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: VFSC Registered Agent and Company Secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm the physical registered office address at the approved agent's premises in Port Vila or Luganville. Establish the statutory registers, minute book, share registry, and charges register. File the change of registered office form if any later move occurs.
required_dossiers: Consent to act as registered agent
Board resolution on registered office adoption
Statutory registers and corporate record binder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If VFSC does not accept the registered office address, select another registered office provider, execute a new consent form, and file Form IC-14 (Notice of Registered Office) with VFSC; the effective date is the date of acceptance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company Directors, Company Secretary, and VFSC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first board meeting or pass written resolutions confirming share subscriptions, registered office, officers, and banking institution. Ensure annual returns are filed with VFSC 15 days after each anniversary. For the proposed LegalTech SaaS business, no economic substance license is triggered because the company is not carrying on financial, securities, or fiduciary business.
required_dossiers: Minutes or written resolutions of the first board of directors
Certificate of Incorporation and constitutional documents
Annual return calendar and VFSC annual fee notice
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: For late annual return or governance filing, pay the late penalty and file VFSC Form AR-1; material failures may be cured by a formal director's declaration and voluntary disclosure to avoid deregistration.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — ISIC 6201 (cloud document automation and e-signature authentication) has no physical industrial establishment or manufacturing permit requirement.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None required — the legal entity will operate as a pure digital services company with no premises-based operational license beyond standard business registration.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Vanuatu Environment Unit, Department of Environmental Protection and Conservation (Ministry of Climate Change Adaptation, Meteorology, Geo-Hazards, Environment, Energy and Disaster Management)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no environmental impact assessment is triggered for a software-as-a-service company with no construction, land disturbance, discharge pipeline, or industrial plant.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No baseline discharge thresholds apply at formation. The company should maintain a zero-discharge profile for wastewater, VOCs, and solid waste. If cloud servers are provisioned, environmental compliance is handled by the data center provider, and the company must adopt a WEEE-compliant e-waste policy for any office or customer-premises hardware.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not required for a remote digital services entity. If an office lease is later entered into, the landlord must provide a fire safety certificate from the National Fire Service, a structural inspection clearance for the building, and a workplace safety induction under the Health and Safety at Work Act. No manufacturing clearance is applicable.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Vanuatu Revenue and Customs (VRC), Ministry of Finance and Economic Management; taxpayer portal at https://vrc.gov.vu; company registry at Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC), https://www.vfsc.vu
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Incorporate the International Company (IC) with VFSC under the International Companies Act Cap 222 via a licensed local registered agent (same-day or next-day incorporation); 2) Obtain the Certificate of Incorporation, Company Code, and stamped Memorandum and Articles of Association; 3) Pay the annual VFSC business licence fee (flat fee, revenue-independent, mandatory for every IC); 4) Apply to VRC for VAT registration ONLY if the IC makes taxable supplies in Vanuatu exceeding VUV 5,000,000 in any 12-month period or voluntarily opts in; an offshore-only SaaS platform (ISIC 6201) exporting to non-residents is not VAT-registrable and requires no VRC TIN; 5) No income-tax TIN, no employer PAYE registration, and no corporate income-tax filing obligation exist for ICs under the Vanuatu zero-corporate-tax regime.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Vanuatu has no check-the-box, US S-corp, or hybrid-mismatch entity classification election. An International Company automatically receives the unconditional statutory tax exemption under Section 148 of the International Companies Act Cap 222 (no tax on income, assets, capital gains, dividends, interest, or royalties). For VAT purposes, an IC may elect voluntary registration under the VAT Act Cap 248 even below the VUV 5,000,000 threshold, and may elect zero-rating for exported services to non-resident recipients; conversely it may elect to remain wholly outside the VAT net by supplying only offshore services.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: VUV 5,000,000 (approximately USD 41,700) of annual taxable supplies made within or connected to Vanuatu; an International Company whose entire business is the export of LegalTech SaaS services to non-resident customers has no Vanuatu VAT nexus and is neither required nor eligible to register in respect of those offshore revenues
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: None. Vanuatu does not currently mandate real-time fiscal clearance, API-based e-invoicing, digital stamping, or clearance-server validation. VAT invoices must be issued in paper or PDF format and contain the statutory fields prescribed by the VAT Act Cap 248 Section 25; VRC operates an IFMIS modernisation programme but no third-party electronic invoice clearance obligation exists as of the current tax year.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available under the VAT Act Cap 248 for (a) goods physically exported from Vanuatu evidenced by customs documentation, and (b) services supplied to a recipient who is not resident in Vanuatu and who consumes the services wholly outside Vanuatu, provided no local economic use arises; qualifying categories expressly include cloud document automation, e-signature authentication, and other digital business-to-business services delivered offshore. The IC must retain proof that the recipient is non-resident, that payment originates offshore, and that the service is not enjoyed in Vanuatu; input VAT credits may be claimed on costs attributable to zero-rated export activity where the IC is VAT-registered.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: ASYCUDA World Customs Export Declaration (XGD) with customs receipt or export clearance stamp
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing export movement (goods)
Non-resident customer agreement / SaaS subscription terms and delivery records (services)
Foreign-currency bank statement or wire transfer advice evidencing inbound settlement (no formal Inward Remittance Certificate exists in Vanuatu due to the absence of exchange controls)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: VRC audit review focuses on export substantiation, non-resident counter-party identity, and absence of local consumption. Fraudulent or erroneous zero-rating claims, false VAT refund claims, or misuse of the IC export exemption trigger: (i) civil assessment of underpaid VAT plus a civil penalty of up to 200% of the VAT evaded; (ii) criminal liability under the VAT Act Cap 248 with fines of up to VUV 1,000,000 and imprisonment for up to seven years; (iii) retrospective clawback of input VAT credits and export refunds plus interest; and (iv) administrative sanctions by VFSC including deregistration or strike-off of the International Company for abuse of the tax-exempt licence. Although the IC itself has no corporate income-tax exposure, inaccurate export declarations may also attract Customs offences under the Customs Act and material prejudice to annual VFSC licence renewal.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of Vanuatu (RBV) acting under the Exchange Control Act [Cap 68] and the AML/CFT statutory framework, in conjunction with the Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) for licensing and corporate compliance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Vanuatu vatu (VUV) is freely convertible for current account and most capital account transactions. There are no general currency convertibility restrictions on profit remittance, dividend distribution, loan repayments, or repatriation of foreign direct investment. Inward and outward payments are not subject to routine prior central bank approval, but authorized dealer banks must apply customer due diligence and statistical reporting thresholds under RBV regulations and the Exchange Control Act. Capital account flows are treated as permissible unless the transaction implicates UN/OFAC sanctions, anti-money-laundering suspicion, or a false trade declaration.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory mandate exists requiring surrender of export proceeds to the central bank and no minimum percentage of foreign currency earnings must be converted into VUV. Exporters may maintain foreign currency accounts with licensed banks in Vanuatu. However, all export receipts must be reported to the authorized dealer bank for statistical balance-of-payments purposes, and substantial cash transactions must be declared to the RBV Financial Intelligence Unit under the AML/CFT regime. Non-compliance with reporting may result in administrative penalties.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational multi-currency account (VUV/USD/AUD) and capital injection clearing account
General corporate operating account and escrow-capable deposit account
Corporate current account and term-deposit backed treasury line

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of South Pacific (BSP) Vanuatu Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Retail and corporate settlement account with Pacific-wide correspondent reach

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low to Medium. Vanuatu does not regulate foreign electronic money institutions (EMIs) as a separate passportable class. Offshore EMIs can generally be used to acquire SaaS card payments and to facilitate cross-border payouts in USD/EUR/GBP without a Vanuatu banking license, provided they do not hold themselves out as carrying on banking business in Vanuatu. However, tier-1 Vanuatu banks treat unregulated EMI balances with heightened source-of-funds scrutiny and may reject them for primary treasury settlement. A licensed card acquirer and a recognized correspondent bank are preferred for the LegalTech SaaS model.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: There is no statutory obligation for every director to appear physically in a branch for account opening. However, RBV AML/CFT guidelines and standard commercial bank underwriting generally require at least one director or an authorized signatory to undergo an in-person or equivalent electronic identity verification interview onshore. Remote individual directors may be onboarded using notarized passport copies, bank-confirmed identity verification, and a board resolution explicitly approving their authority. Some banks, as a risk instinct, still require the local resident agent or a director to visit the branch for initial account activation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner or director is politically exposed (PEP) or appears on a sanctions/negative-news list.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Negative media search report, government-issued identity documents, source-of-wealth declaration with supporting asset title or audited financials, PEP disposition statement, corporate board resolution approving account opening, and confirmation from the VFSC that no disqualification orders exist.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of funds for the initial capital contribution or the first 90 days of SaaS revenue.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Capital contribution ledger, signed shareholder subscription agreement, seed-funding or venture capital term sheet, three months of personal or corporate bank statements, executed client subscription agreements for the SaaS e-signature product, and a three-year cash-flow forecast describing expected incoming wire volumes.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border counterparties include jurisdictions or virtual-asset intermediaries that trigger enhanced due diligence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: An organizational chart of all counterparties and beneficial owners, certificates of incorporation or good standing, a description of the exact payment flow, valid third-party due diligence reports, legal opinions from the counterparty's counsel if needed, and a written AML policy prepared for the Vanuatu International Company.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payment rails are dominated by Stripe and card settlement rather than commercial bank wire transfers, raising uncertainty about treasury provenance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Merchant acquiring agreement with a licensed payment processor, PCI DSS attestation of compliance, settlement schedule and chargeback policy, a bank-authenticated copy of the Stripe payout statements, and an internal reconciliation policy proving that card settlements are independently identified before payment to beneficiaries.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity capital transfers must be routed through an authorized dealer bank in Vanuatu using the SWIFT MT103 message format. The sending bank should use purpose field code describing equity injection or intercompany capital contribution; common international purpose codes include 6010 (FDI equity) or a descriptive text consistent with OECD Balance of Payments classification. The recipient Vanuatu bank will require a board resolution, a copy of the investment agreement, the International Company's certificate of incorporation, beneficial ownership declaration, and, for sums exceeding statutory thresholds, an AML source-of-funds statement. No prior RBV exchange control approval is required, but the receiving bank must register the transaction in its balance-of-payments reporting to the Reserve Bank.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements for SaaS licensing, professional fees, and cloud infrastructure costs should be executed via SWIFT MT103 messages using correspondent clearing through ANZ/BRED and their global intermediaries. A commercial letter of credit is generally unsuitable for intangible services, so documentary collection is customarily replaced by a bank-to-bank wire against invoices and electronic acceptance certificates. For high-value settlements in USD or EUR, the treasury may use correspondent bank accounts at JPMorgan, Citibank, or BNP Paribas via the Vanuatu bank's nostril account network; intraday liquidity discipline should be maintained by pre-funding the operating account one day prior to scheduled outbound payments.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanuatu vatu/USD deliverable forward contracts with licensed commercial banks onshore, provided the underlying commercial exposure is evidenced by signed SaaS contracts or supplier invoices.
Cross-currency swaps between VUV and USD/AUD/EUR executed through a licensed authorized dealer bank for treasury risk management, subject to the new ISDA/CPS standard master agreement.

Offshore non-deliverable forward (NDF) contracts referencing VUV, permitted for Vanuatu corporates when used solely to hedge expected non-VUV cash flows and when the counterparty is a reputable investment-grade bank; no onshore NDF market exists.

Foreign exchange option collars or vanilla options on USD/VUV offered by the local commercial bank treasury desks, possible when bilateral credit limits are established and the positive accounting treatment is confirmed under IFRS 9 hedge accounting.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual International Company Government Fee Renewal and Registered Agent Certification
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) via licensed registered agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On each anniversary of incorporation; grace period of 2 months from due date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late penalty of VUV 10,000 (approx. USD 85) plus 10% of annual fee per month or part; continued non-payment leads to administrative strike-off and loss of separate legal personality

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filed Financial Statement (for records, not publicly lodged; retained at registered office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered agent / registered office in Vanuatu
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the anniversary of each financial year or as set by board resolution
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No filing penalty, but failure to maintain records constitutes an offence under VIC Act Cap 222, subject to fine of not exceeding VUV 1,000,000 (approx. USD 8,400); no strike-off for this item alone

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaration of Issued Capital and Shareholding (submitted by registered agent alongside license renewal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Simultaneously with annual government fee payment on incorporation anniversary; no extension normally granted
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Filing is conditional for license renewal; omission triggers conditional resolution for strike-off, then compulsory strike-off within 6 months

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit required for International Companies irrespective of size or turnover; audit only if shareholder resolution voluntarily requests independent review
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: No prescribed GAAP under Vanuatu International Companies Act; company may maintain records under IFRS, US GAAP, or other internationally accepted standards

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No public UBO registry or annual UBO confirmation obligation in Vanuatu. However, all share transfers must be recorded in the Register of Members and the change of beneficial ownership reflected in the registered agent's internal file. The registered agent must annually confirm the accuracy of its recorded beneficial ownership data for AML/CFT purposes.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% (Vanuatu levies no corporate income tax, capital gains tax, or withholding tax at the national level)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: International Company (IC) tax-exempt status under the Vanuatu International Companies Act: full exemption from income tax on all international business income, no capital gains tax on share disposals, and no tax on dividends or interest derived by non-resident shareholders.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: N/A – No corporate income tax return exists. The annual compliance filing is the VFSC Annual Return / License Renewal lodged through a licensed registered agent via the Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) e-filing portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual license fee and third-party confirmation must be filed within 30 days after the anniversary of incorporation. The VFSC grants a 30-day grace period; failure to comply triggers late fees and potential striking-off.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered agent confirmation of the IC's registered office and principal address in Vanuatu.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident ICs must maintain a registered office in Vanuatu at the registered agent's address; a foreign service address for business operations may be disclosed in the International Company Register.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Shareholder and director details, including beneficial ownership information.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All shareholder and director names, nationalities, and addresses must be submitted to the registered agent. The agent is obligated to maintain but not publicly file beneficial ownership data unless requested by VFSC.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Share capital and issuance statement confirming no public subscription in Vanuatu.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If shares are issued to non-residents, no tax declaration is required because the IC is tax-exempt. Keep a share register at the registered office.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late lodgment of the VFSC annual license fee incurs a penalty of VT 25,000 (approximately USD 210). Continued non-payment after 3 months leads to automatic strike-off from the International Companies Register, forfeiture of assets to the Crown, and loss of the corporate veil for subsequent contracts.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% (no dividend withholding tax imposed by Vanuatu)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Vanuatu has no comprehensive double taxation agreements (DTAs) with major economies. Consequently, no treaty clearance or Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) procedure exists for dividend relief. The IC is not a tax resident of Vanuatu for income tax purposes; a Certificate of Good Standing from VFSC can be issued to satisfy foreign counterparties.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory: 0% withholding on cross-border royalties and interest. Treaty: N/A (no DTA network). Foreign-source payments received by the IC are outside Vanuatu's taxation jurisdiction.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No statutory transfer pricing documentation threshold under Vanuatu law because no corporate income tax regime exists. However, the Vanuatu Economic Substance Regulations require a filing for ICs engaged in geographically mobile activities if the IC is treated as tax resident in Vanuatu; the gross income threshold for ESR designation is 3,000,000 Vatu (approx. USD 25,000) per annum.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Vanuatu's Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) apply to companies tax resident in Vanuatu. A Vanuatu International Company is generally non-resident if its central management and control are outside Vanuatu. If the IC is controlled from Vanuatu, ESR requires physical presence, local employees, and expenditure proportionate to the income from covered activities. For remote/digital LegalTech SaaS operations, the covered activity test typically fails if no core income-generating functions are performed in Vanuatu.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Misrepresenting the IC's tax-exempt status while maintaining central management and control inside Vanuatu, or deriving local Vanuatu-source income without disclosure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine of up to VT 5,000,000 (approx. USD 42,000) and/or imprisonment for up to 12 months under the International Companies Act and Income Tax (Amendment) provisions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be jointly and severally liable for unpaid taxes and penalties if they knowingly authorized the false tax-exemption claim; a criminal conviction can trigger a travel ban and asset forfeiture.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Registering an IC solely as a holding shell without any commercial operation, revenue, or disclosure of substantial electronic services, while claiming tax-exempt status to avoid foreign substance requirements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Strike-off from the International Companies Register, voiding of all contracts signed under the IC, and a direct VFSC fine of VT 200,000 (approx. USD 1,700) for failure to supply economic substance information.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face personal restoration orders for all liabilities incurred after the IC became shell in substance; revocation of the right to act as a director of any Vanuatu company for 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain a beneficial ownership register or knowingly misreporting the ultimate beneficial owner of the LegalTech SaaS business through the Vanuatu registered agent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal penalty of up to VT 10,000,000 (approx. USD 85,000) and imprisonment of up to 15 years under the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for AML penalties and are prohibited from leaving Vanuatu pending investigation; foreign directors may face extradition assistance requests.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Illegal Dividend or Return of Capital
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing profits to shareholders while the IC is insolvent or using the tax-exempt status to evade obligations to third-party SaaS subscribers, such as refunds or warranty liabilities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Excess distribution voidable; director liability for the full amount distributed plus interest. VFSC may order restoration of corporate records and a public reprimand.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors become personally liable for reprobating debts; in cases of fraudulent trading, civil restitution is extended to family trusts or related underlying companies, and imprisonment up to 7 years may be imposed.
